page: Microsoft Azure D8ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The server is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

For local storage, the D8ads_v6 includes a bundled 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance and memory write bandwidth for large blocks fall within the average range. However, a notable performance tradeoff is observed in uncached large-block read memory bandwidth, which registers at 38.94 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25%. Additionally, while text processing performance is strong, medium-model (7B) LLM prompt processing is relatively weak at 23.56 tokens/sec.

Given its hardware profile and balanced resource allocation, the D8ads_v6 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources and fast local scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing, 32 GB of RAM, and local NVMe storage makes this instance well-suited for general-purpose workloads, relational databases, web serving, text processing, and software compilation tasks.
